newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn dismisses report of "unsafe" missiles.
newsitem.headline: Bonn dismisses report of "unsafe" missiles.

text.p: Defence Minister Volker Ruehe on Friday dismissed a television report that the German air force and its allies were using an unsafe missile system which posed a danger to their troops and the civilian population.
Ruehe said the allegations about the HARM (High Speed Anti-Radiation Missile) system in ARD television's Panorama programme were "not tenable".

Panorama said a secret defence ministry report had alleged that the missiles, made by Texas Instruments of the United States and intended to lock on to enemy radar systems, were dangerously unreliable.

The programme said that when deployed for peacekeeping in the Bosnian conflict, the air-launched missiles had twice missed their targets and gone on to explode in Hungary. It was unclear if the missiles had been fired by German, Italian or U.S. forces.
Ruehe said the sophisticated technology of the Tornado jets which carry the missiles minimised the risk of errors and that the HARM system was the most modern of its type.
"The capabilities and limits of this weapon were known. They were incorrectly portrayed and wrongly evaluated in the programme," the minister said in a statement.

He said the German air force had not fired a single HARM missile in Bosnia and that the system had an important deterrent effect, as the enemy often did not dare to switch on its radar for fear of providing the missiles with a target.
